recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Motion in a Straight Line · 4 marks

steps.label: Eliminate t
lines: From v = u + at,  t = (v − u)/a.
steps.why: The two standard equations both contain t, so eliminating t between them produces a relation that connects v, u, a and s alone.
common_mistakes: Squaring only the numerator of (v − u)/a and forgetting the a² underneath.

recall.must_convey: That t is eliminated by substituting t equals v minus u over a into s equals u t plus half a t squared.

steps.memory_tip: Make t the subject of v = u + at, then put it into the s equation.
steps.margin_note: Two marks. Show the substitution before simplifying.

steps.label: The result
steps.why: The cross terms 2uv cancel, which is what leaves a clean relation between the squares of the velocities.
common_mistakes: Losing the factor 2 on the as term.

recall.must_convey: That the result is v squared equals u squared plus two a s.
accept: v squared equals u squared plus two a s
reject: v squared equals u squared plus a s

steps.memory_tip: The 2uv terms cancel. That cancellation is the tidy part.
steps.margin_note: Show the cancellation rather than jumping to the box.

steps.label: When to use it
lines: This equation contains no t, so it is the one
to use whenever the time is neither given
nor asked for, such as finding a stopping
steps.why: Choosing the equation that leaves out the unknown you do not need turns a two-step problem into a one-step problem.
common_mistakes: Using it to find a time. There is no t in it.

recall.must_convey: That the equation has no t, so it is used when time is not given and not asked for.

steps.memory_tip: No t anywhere. Use it whenever time is not part of the question.
steps.margin_note: One sentence on when to reach for it.

insider_note: This is the equation with no t in it. Say that — it is why the examiner asks for it separately.
